glossary.definition: A separate service that a gateway asks to inspect the text of an agent or LLM request and response. It answers with findings; the gateway, not the sidecar, decides to allow or block. In this demo the sidecar is a small loopback-only HTTP service with a deterministic stand-in detector.

A per-category severity (low, medium, high, or none) at or above which the gateway blocks. A finding below it is allowed, with an alert. A category set to none never blocks (observe-only). The values in this demo are demo choices, not product defaults.

What the gateway does when the sidecar errors (502) or does not answer in time. Fail closed blocks every request, even harmless ones. Fail open lets every request through unchecked, even an attack. The toggle is called Sidecar Fail Closed in the environment this demo was modelled on.

The sidecar's answer to /inspect: a list of { category, severity, location.index, messages, contents }. An empty list means allow. In this demo contents are masked and made inert, so a finding never echoes a full SSN or card number.

Every string a user or agent supplies is treated as data: hidden characters are shown as [U+XXXX], sizes are bounded, the UI renders it as a text node and never as HTML, and nothing in it is evaluated or followed.

The request { tenant, user, app_name, units: [ { role, direction, text } ] } and the response { findings }. As understood from the demo environment and UNVERIFIED against product documentation: it was reverse-engineered, and this demo does not check it against anything.

Ping release claim, UNVERIFIED on our tenant: "your own formats paste in unchanged". In this app you paste rules with id, description, regex, keywords, entropy, secretGroup, category, severity and an allowlist; one bad rule refuses the whole paste; patterns are checked before they run and the pattern is never shown back. The key names are the app's reading of the gitleaks format.

A guardrail attached to the calling agent's key, so two callers sending the same A2A message can be treated differently: one enforcing, one observe-only. As understood from the demo environment; unverified here.

Ping release claim, UNVERIFIED on our tenant: detection is per kind, numeric kinds are checksum-validated, and your own formats can be pasted. In this app each kind is a regex plus a check digit or a structural check, you choose which kinds raise a finding (the original five by default), and every kind is masked in anything shown. The kind list is this app's own, not Ping's.

A detector for personal data scanned on both the request and the response direction. Here it is regex plus a check digit where one exists (Luhn for cards, mod 97 for IBAN-shaped values, and others) over a catalogue of this app's own illustrative kinds. You choose which kinds raise a finding; the original five (SSN, card, email, phone, IBAN-shaped) are on by default, and every kind is masked in anything shown whatever is chosen. It is not Presidio and it finds well-formed values, not every kind of personal data.

glossary.term: Ping's release numbers versus this app's
glossary.definition: Ping release claim, UNVERIFIED on our tenant. Ping's deck (slide 53) says 23 personal-data kinds (up from 5), 364 secret and credential detectors, 47 behavioural rules and 411 maintained rules in total. Those are Ping's figures, uncited in the deck and not measured by us. This app ships its own smaller illustrative sets (11 kinds, 12 secret detectors), computed from its engine and never presented as Ping's.

glossary.term: Prompt logging sealed to your key
glossary.definition: Ping release claim, UNVERIFIED on our tenant: prompts and responses can be retained encrypted with a public key you supply, and the vendor never holds the private half. In this app the server seals each run to your X25519 public key (ephemeral key, HKDF-SHA256, AES-256-GCM: the envelope is the app's own invention), who and what was decided stay in the clear, nothing is recorded without a public key, and a record opens only in the page with a private key you hold. The server has no decrypt code.
Inspecting what the model answers, not only what the user asked. A clean request can still produce a response that leaks personal data; only scanning the response direction stops that.

A deterministic set of keyword and pattern rules with a score from 0 to 1, used here in place of a real classifier. It is not a model and learns nothing. It misses a paraphrased attack and flags a harmless sentence on purpose, to show that detection quality is a property of the model you deploy. This app makes no claim about real product detection quality, defaults or licensing.

The contract and the gateway behaviour in this demo are as understood from the demo environment, UNVERIFIED against product documentation. Check the product documentation before relying on any detail.

Ping claims, UNVERIFIED on our tenant. Challenge: Authorization cannot see content: an agent following hidden instructions can exfiltrate data within policy. Technical: Content inspected in and out across MCP, A2A, LLM and coding-agent traffic; deterministic rules add no availability dependency. Business: A fraction of the cost of one incident; framework-mapped evidence for AI governance sign-off.

glossary.term: Why it matters: Prompt Logging (deck slide 50)
glossary.definition: Ping claims, UNVERIFIED on our tenant. Challenge: Retaining prompts is what investigations need and what teams refuse to hand a vendor. Technical: Content sealed to your public key, decrypted only in your console session; Privilege never holds the private half. Business: Forensic retention becomes acceptable to security and legal.

cards.label: The /inspect contract
cards.description: Units in, findings out, as understood from the demo environment and unverified against product documentation.

cards.label: H2 2026: personal-data kinds and secret detectors
cards.description: Ping release claim, UNVERIFIED on our tenant. Choose which personal-data kinds raise a finding, see each check digit proved on a valid sample and a near miss, and try the app's own secret detectors. Ping's counts are quoted from its deck, never presented as the app's.

cards.label: H2 2026: prompt logging sealed to your key
cards.description: Ping release claim, UNVERIFIED on our tenant. Make a key pair in the browser, seal each run to the public half on the server, and open a record in the page with the private half.

cards.label: H2 2026: paste your own gitleaks-format rules
cards.description: Ping release claim, UNVERIFIED on our tenant. Paste rules in the gitleaks format; one bad rule refuses the whole paste and nothing is added.

cards.label: Break the sidecar: fail closed vs fail open
cards.description: Inject a 502, a timeout or a slow answer and compare what the gateway does in each mode.

cards.label: Run the scripted scenarios
cards.description: Benign prompt, direct injection, PII in a request, PII leaking in a response, and an A2A message through two keys. Watch the gateway allow or block.

cards.label: What the stand-in misses
cards.description: A paraphrased attack the stand-in allows and a harmless sentence it blocks. Detection quality belongs to the model.

stories.title: The gateway sends text
stories.say: The text units of an agent or LLM request, and later of the response, go to the sidecar's /inspect.

stories.title: The sidecar answers with findings
stories.say: Each finding has a category, a severity and the index of the unit it is about. An empty list means allow.

stories.title: The gateway compares
stories.say: A finding at or above that category's block threshold means block. Otherwise it allows, maybe with an alert.

stories.title: If the sidecar fails
stories.say: A Fail Closed toggle decides: block everything, or let everything through unchecked.
